<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/service-analytics`, touching **28** documentable anchor(s).

**26** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 035a12cc248fe38610f2cb1e37d4aaeacae568c8`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `objectName (symbol, 59 pages)`
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **27** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 035a12cc248fe38610f2cb1e37d4aaeacae568c8` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `615f989f307ff96f1315ec58a318b22563da8b69` — the merge of head `948f9983194a829ab2c7f35d11a4fed941908431` into base `035a12cc248fe38610f2cb1e37d4aaeacae568c8`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 615f989f307ff96f1315ec58a318b22563da8b69 && git checkout 615f989f307ff96f1315ec58a318b22563da8b69
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 035a12cc248fe38610f2cb1e37d4aaeacae568c8 948f9983194a829ab2c7f35d11a4fed941908431 && git checkout -B drift-repro 035a12cc248fe38610f2cb1e37d4aaeacae568c8 && git merge --no-ff 948f9983194a829ab2c7f35d11a4fed941908431

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 035a12cc248fe38610f2cb1e37d4aaeacae568c8
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 035a12cc248fe38610f2cb1e37d4aaeacae568c8` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## L1 · PR #36060 · head `f01bd3db4e8ba25f7bc4e7b011a5e706bce7d4da` · **REWORK** (declaration and filing only, no code change asked) · 2026-11-21T12:38Z

Card #35491 (p2, area d7-D). Requested by the area thread with this head as the final green head. Claim: 7061790933. Dev report: 7062353045. I read the full diff: 11 files, +1032/−11.

### Face
- `l1-face.mjs --pr 36060` is CLEAN at `f01bd3db4e`: open draft on `main`, first line `Fixes #35491`, no closing keyword on another card, one changeset for `@objectstack/objectql` and `@objectstack/service-analytics` (patch), Lint & Repo Gates and TypeScript Type Check `success`, all check-runs 38 success / 0 failed / 0 pending, mergeable clean.
- Files stay inside the claim's surface.

### The code: sound, a faithful mirror
- **`record-unit-aggregate-door.ts` (ObjectQL).**
  - It judges `sum`/`avg`/`min`/`max` (ADR-0144 Open item 10's set) over a `number` with `unitConfig.unitMode: 'record'`. `groupBy` admits the unit field as a name or as `{ field }`. It throws `INVALID_FIELD`/400 before any driver is asked.
  - It sits after the currency door in `DeleteAndAggregateFacet`.
  - No roll-up channel is needed: L3 admits no roll-up over such a quantity.
- **`recordUnitSummaryRefusal`.** It refuses `INVALID_METADATA`/422, whichever end registers second, a self roll-up included; `count` is admitted. The pins assert `code` and `status` (ADR-0112).
- **`cube-record-unit-door.ts`.** It is line-for-line the currency door's judgment, minus the home-field remedy, which has no twin. It is wired at all four `assertRecordCurrencyGrouped` call sites: the draft preview at l.3244, the ad-hoc exit, the augmented cube and the declared cube.
- **`groupedColumnOf`.** This is the currency door's dimension resolver moved verbatim into a shared private method; no currency behaviour moves.
- **Tests.** Refusals are pinned per function, per strategy, for the cube face, the inferred cube, a `totals` grand total and the draft preview, each with a no-read check. Grouped answers are right per unit. `count`/`count_distinct`, a fixed-mode quantity and a plain `number` are served.
- **Evidence.**
  - The dev's ablation per door turns 2, 3 and 17 tests red.
  - Package suites: objectql 14223, service-analytics 5674.
  - I did not re-run locally. The check-runs at this head (Test Core included) are the gate witness.

### R1 (must fix): the declaration is `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, not `no`
The claim's basis is that `unitConfig` has not shipped, so no published accept set narrows. That is true for the narrowing arm, but the diff also widens a published surface.

- `AnalyticsServiceConfig` is a root type export of `@objectstack/service-analytics` (`src/index.ts` l.5). Its `sourceFieldMeta` answer gains one optional key, `unitField`, which `AnalyticsServicePlugin` now relays.
- The exact precedent is a35fc66 in `packages/services/service-analytics/CHANGELOG.md` (l.415–423). It added `homeAmountField` to the same answer and declared `Clause-②: yes (widening)` / `Metadata-protocol: none`, with a **The widening.** bullet.
- The thrown errors also gain a `unitField` property (both doors). Say whether that reaches the wire envelope; if it does, it is an answer member and belongs in the same bullet.
- The test (`execution-duties.md`): does the card widen an accept set or the public surface. Yes.

Asked:
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` / `Metadata-protocol: none` in the PR body and in the changeset body. Patch stays right: a non-protocol widening ships patch (AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3).
- A widening bullet in the changeset naming the key, and the error member if it reaches the wire.
- A claim correction on #35491 carrying the line-initial `Clause-②: yes`. The Clause-② queue gate reads only the claim's line-initial key.
- **L2 follows.** `Clause-②: yes` makes a contract review owed at `TIER_DEFAULT` (`contract-review.md`). L1-b runs it as an isolated subagent once the redeclared head is announced. A changeset-only fix moves the head on the prose face only.

### R2 (must fix before ACCEPT): two out-of-scope findings need a filing-gate pass and a line in Acceptance notes
1. **The UI consumers of a whole-set aggregate (the unit twin of #32334).**
   - Today `useWholeSetSummary` / `compileWholeSetSummaryQuery` (`ui/packages/plugin-grid`) send a column `summary: 'sum'` as one ungrouped aggregate over the whole filter.
   - `recordCurrencyAggregates.ts` (`requiredCurrencyGrouping`, `honestGroupAggregations`) and `useColumnSummary` skip only record-mode currency. No `ui/**` file reads `unitConfig` at all.
   - Once this refusal ships, a grid or list view summing a record-mode quantity column gets the whole query refused. Every other summarised column in that view then falls back to a page total under a whole-view label, and grouped views drop their group aggregates the same way. That is the #32334 defect, now on quantities. Read from code, not run.
   - The PR's repo-wide sweep grepped `unitMode: 'record'` declarations; it could not see these generic callers.
   - Landing: `ui/packages/plugin-grid` (domain:ui). It should land before `unitConfig` ships in a release, so both reach users together.
2. **Dataset build-time half and derived measures.**
   - The card's Done-when says a dataset is "refused at build with a named code".
   - ADR-0144's dated note defines "at build" for a dataset measure as "at compile … `DATASET_INVALID`". That holds for both families, since ADR-0158 U7 R1 mirrors D6.
   - The PR mirrors what currency actually does on main: per selection, `INVALID_FIELD` at the cube door. That is the area's option A, and I accept it as a deviation for this PR: it is the built twin, every selection is judged, and nothing reads. It still leaves the ADR text and main apart for both families.
   - Protocol first (code to the ADR by default), so file one card for a `DATASET_INVALID` compile guard covering both families, plus the derived-measure twin of currency guard 2.
   - Note the asymmetry for whoever ranks it. Before `unitConfig` ships, the unit half is no narrowing. Once it ships, the unit half becomes a narrowing, as the currency half already is (ADR-0087 disposition).

The PR keeps `Fixes #35491`. The build-time dataset half moves to the card from item 2; the seat decides that routing. The remaining two Acceptance notes are fine as written: the two-segment `unitField` and the sweep.

### Changeset sentences (read against the diff)
All five statements are true of the code: the before reading; the engine door with code, status and message contents; the summary at 422, whichever registers second, with `count` the remedy; analytics on every cube path, `totals` and the draft preview, with `unitField` relayed only under `record` on a `number`; and the not-judged list with no new error code. One sentence needs to change: the declaration line (R1). The widening bullet is to be added.

### carrier
`carrier:` ADR-0158 Open item 12, the aggregate half resolved by this PR. After merge, the landing seat appends that line on the open "ADR revisions, week of …" card (`execution-duties.md`). It is not in this PR.

### Next
Delta L1 on the redeclared head and the two filings (ids in the Acceptance notes), then the TIER_DEFAULT L2 from L1-b.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `948f9983194a829ab2c7f35d11a4fed941908431`
Local-runs: none

Rendered 2026-11-21T12:49Z by an isolated reviewer sub-agent at TIER_DEFAULT (brief in the next comment), adopted by the L1-b session.

Face: declaration (`Clause-②: yes (widening)`, claim amendment 7062726625). The committed tree touches no `packages/spec/src/**` and no governed path (11 files: one changeset, two ADR anchors, four objectql and four service-analytics source and test files). Inputs read: card #35491 body and all five comments, PR #36060 body and file list, the net diff `origin/main...pr/36060` (merge-base `8145424b53`), and the head's check-runs. Author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no author note is owed.

### ① Derived judgments

1. `AnalyticsServiceConfig.sourceFieldMeta` answer gains the optional key `unitField?: string`. `AnalyticsServiceConfig` is a root type export (`export type { AnalyticsServiceConfig }` in `packages/services/service-analytics/src/index.ts`; the package `exports` map has only `.`), and the key sits on a host-supplied callback's return type, so a host that omits it is unchanged: a published widening. **Right**, and it is the one published-surface change, as the PR body and changeset say.
2. `AnalyticsServicePlugin` now relays `unitField` for a `number` under `unitMode: 'record'` with a non-empty string, and for nothing else (`plugin.ts`). Behaviour behind item 1, same shape as its `homeAmountField` relay. **Right.**
3. `ObjectQL.aggregate` accept set: `sum` / `avg` / `min` / `max` over a `number` field with `unitConfig.unitMode: 'record'` is refused `INVALID_FIELD` / 400 unless `groupBy` (string or `{ field }` entry) includes its `unitField`; asked right after the record-currency door, before any driver. This narrows only what a `record`-mode quantity accepts, and that declaration is unreleased: on `origin/main` `1c879568c4` `packages/spec` is 18.6.0, its `CHANGELOG.md` carries no `unitConfig` or `unitMode`, and `.changeset/35489-unit-config.md` is still pending. So no published accept set narrows. **Right** (no `(narrowing)` arm owed), on the condition the PR states: if a release ships `unitConfig` before this merges, the declaration must be redone as `no (narrowing)`.
4. `SchemaRegistry` registration accept set: a `summary` rolling up `sum` / `avg` / `min` / `max` of a `record`-mode child quantity is refused `INVALID_METADATA` / 422 (`RecordUnitSummaryRefusedError`), judged at whichever registration completes the pair, and over a self roll-up. Same unreleased basis as item 3, so `Metadata-protocol: none` holds. **Right.** It sits after the `opts.bodyOnly` return, exactly as its currency twin does.
5. Analytics cube accept set: the same four aggregates over such a quantity are refused `INVALID_FIELD` / 400 unless a dimension's column is the `unitField` on the same object, at all four places that ask the currency door (inferred, augmented and declared `ensureCube` paths, the draft-preview branch). Same unreleased basis. **Right.** Stand-downs (no `sourceFieldMeta`, non-bare `cube.sql`, unresolvable member) are line for line the currency helper's.
6. No new public symbol: `recordUnitFieldOf`, `assertRecordUnitAggregatesGrouped`, `readsRecordUnitQuantity`, `RecordUnitSummaryRefusedError`, `RECORD_UNIT_SUMMARY_REFUSED_CODE` and `QUANTITY_AGGREGATES` are not re-exported from objectql `.` or `./core` (`src/core.ts`) or from service-analytics `.`, and `judgeRegistrationDoors` stays typed `{ refusal: Error }`, so the new class is not reachable from an entry's type graph. **Right.**
7. Wire: no new error code (`INVALID_FIELD`, `INVALID_METADATA` from the existing catalog). The thrown errors' `unitField` member is in process only; the PR's measured REST bodies (`/data` keeps `field` and `object`; analytics keeps `code` and `message`) show no envelope change. **Right**, not part of the widening.
8. `groupedColumnOf` extraction in `analytics-service.ts`: the removed inline resolver and the new private method are textually identical; no accept-set change. **Right.**

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/35491-unit-raw-aggregate.md`: `patch` for `@objectstack/objectql` and `@objectstack/service-analytics`, the only two published packages the diff moves (`scripts/adr-anchors/**` publishes nothing). Both declaration lines are line-initial in the changeset body and in the PR body: `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`. AGENTS.md (Post-Task Checklist 3): a `none` kind takes `patch`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. The level matches what the diff publishes; no `skip-changeset`. The `Check Changeset` check-runs on the head concluded success.

Clause-②: yes (widening) — right: item ① 1 is a widening of a root type export, and items ① 3 to 5 narrow only an unreleased declaration.

### ③ Boundary flags

- open_questions 1 (dataset compile `DATASET_INVALID` for a raw measure with no unit-field dimension; card thread took A). Answered, accepted as a deviation, carried. The card's Done-when says a dataset is "refused at build", and ADR-0144's dated note puts a dataset measure's refusal "at compile" with `DATASET_INVALID`; this PR refuses per query selection (`INVALID_FIELD`), mirroring what main does for currency. The route is recorded on the card (7062776103) with the compile guard for both families moved to #36083. Finding N1 below.
- open_questions 2 (derived measure combining a `record`-mode quantity with another quantity; A). Answered: not a raw aggregate in U7 R1's words, no ruling covers it; carried by #36083 per 7062776103. Accepted.
- out_of_scope_findings 1 ("carrier: none · the ADR-0158 Open item 12 aggregate-half line goes to the weekly ADR revisions card after merge"). Escalated as finding S1 below.
- out_of_scope_findings 2 (objectql pins of the two engine doors share one test file, as their currency twins do). Answered: test layout only, no contract effect.
- Claim amendment 7062726625 (`no` to `yes (widening)`): the new value is the one item ① 1 derives; the narrowing basis still holds at `origin/main` `1c879568c4` (item ① 3).
- `mcp_calls: 0`, `api_writes: 0 by the dev`, `security_findings: none`: nothing to answer.
- SQL push-down (AGENTS.md, Prime Directive 5): no finding. Every door added is a pre-query metadata check over `groupBy`, `aggregations`, cube dimensions and registered schemas; no id is materialised and no join is done in app code. `recordUnitSummaryRefusal`'s scan of registered objects reads metadata only, and only when the incoming body declares a `record`-mode quantity.
- Check-runs on the head at 2026-11-21T12:47Z: **pending, not green**. 54 runs: 14 success, 18 skipped, 1 cancelled (one `PR-body guards (claim · duplicate · Part-of · single-writer path)` run; a second run of the same name concluded success), 21 in progress (`Test Core` 1/10 to 10/10, `Build Core`, the `Type Check ·` and `Lint ·` families, `Live E2E UI`). This PASS covers the contract alone and claims no green: landing still waits for every check to conclude green.

Findings:

- **S1 · should-fix.** The card's Done-when ends "ADR-0158 is amended with the raw-aggregate set", and `Fixes #35491` closes the card at merge. The dev report lists the ADR line as "carrier: none", and the PR body names only an unnumbered "ADR revisions card". When the card closes, that Done-when clause has no numbered carrier, and ADR-0158 Open item 12, the governing text this code answers, stays open with nothing tracking it. To close: name the issue that carries the Open item 12 aggregate-half line (the set as built: `sum`, `avg`, `min`, `max` raw; `count` and `count_distinct` not judged; grouping by the quantity's own `unitField` admits) in the PR body before landing, filing one if none is open. This is a PR-body edit and does not move the head.
- **N1 · nit (accepted deviation, carried).** The dataset half of the card's "refused at build" and ADR-0144's "a dataset measure at compile" are delivered per query, not at compile. No wrong number is served, because every ungrouped selection is refused, and the deviation is recorded on the card and carried by #36083. One ordering point for that carrier: its unit half is not a narrowing only while `unitConfig` is unreleased. If `35489-unit-config.md` ships in a release first, the later compile guard becomes a published narrowing that needs ADR-0087 disposition and maintainer approval. Record that ordering on #36083, as #36082 already records its own.
